new_method.method:
Open Problems: Current image‐classification models are still brittle to *unknown* spurious correlations that were never annotated during training. Existing causal or distributionally-robust approaches either 1) assume environment / group labels (Group-DRO, IRM, ENP), 2) need explicit spurious-attribute tags (AutoACER), or 3) scale poorly to high-resolution images (RSC-MDP, causal RL). Consequently, no method simultaneously (a) avoids any human annotation of spurious factors, (b) scales to ImageNet-level resolution, and (c) provides robustness to *novel* spurious shifts (e.g., totally new backgrounds, texture styles, lighting) that were unseen in training. Solving this self-supervised, high-dimensional spurious-correlation problem would dramatically improve real-world reliability of vision systems.
Methods: We propose "Self-Supervised Counterfactual Vision via Generative Interventions" (SCaRI).
1.  Segmentation-Based Factorization: For every training image, obtain object-foreground masks automatically with Segment-Anything (SAM) or Tokencut. No human labels are required.
2.  Generative Counterfactual Engine: A text-conditioned diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion-Inpainting) is prompted to *replace only the background* or other context attributes while keeping the masked foreground untouched. Prompts are chosen from a library of scene, texture, weather, and lighting descriptions; stochastic sampling yields diverse counterfactuals.
3.  Counterfactual Invariance Training (CIT): For each original image x and its K counterfactuals {x^cf_k}:  
   • Representation Consistency: Using a backbone f_θ (ResNet-50, ViT), enforce ||f_θ(x) – f_θ(x^cf_k)||^2 < ε via an InfoNCE/Barlow Twins style loss.  
   • Prediction Consistency: Cross-entropy on all x and x^cf_k with shared label.  
   • Instance-Adaptive Reweighting: Apply Group-Conditional DRO at the *instance* level by treating (x, {x^cf_k}) as a mini-environment and up-weighting samples whose counterfactual loss is high—no external group labels needed.
4.  Causal Effect Regularizer: Estimate pixel-wise relevance with GAE (for ViTs) or GradCAM. Penalize positive relevance outside the foreground mask (L_bg) and boost relevance inside (L_fg) as in Optimizing Relevance Maps (but using *self-generated* masks).
5.  Fourier-Domain Stabilizer: Add the HFF/CD regularizers from “Models Out of Line” to discourage reliance on high-frequency shortcuts.
The pipeline is end-to-end differentiable; only off-the-shelf SAM and diffusion checkpoints are needed.
Experimental Setup: Datasets:
• Waterbirds, CelebA-Hair (standard spurious benchmarks).  
• ImageNet-9 and Imagenet-A/R/S for natural shifts.  
• ObjectNet-Boxes (bounding-box crops) plus *SCaRI-Synthetic*: we create 50k counterfactual background variants via our diffusion engine to test unseen shifts.

Models: ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 fine-tuned from ImageNet.

Baselines: ERM, Group-DRO (oracle groups), IRM, Mixup, AutoACER (with attribute tags), MoCoDA, ENP (with 5% feature annotations), Fourier-regularized training.

Metrics:
1. ID top-1 accuracy.  
2. Worst-group accuracy (Waterbirds, CelebA).  
3. OOD accuracy on ImageNet-A/R/S, ObjectNet-Boxes, and SCaRI-Synthetic.  
4. Effective-robustness slope (Fourier lens).  
5. Relevance-Foreground Overlap (higher is better).

Ablations: (i) remove diffusion counterfactuals, (ii) remove relevance regularizer, (iii) replace diffusion with simple color jitter, (iv) violin plot accuracy vs. number of generated counterfactuals.

Robustness stress-tests:  
• Background adversarial patches (PatchAttack).  
• Common corruption (ImageNet-C).  
• Feature-space spurious attack: replace background features with those from an unrelated class.
Result: We expect SCaRI to
• Match ERM on ID accuracy (<1% drop).
• Improve worst-group accuracy on Waterbirds from ~72% (ERM) to ≥86%, surpassing Group-DRO w/o group labels.
• Raise OOD accuracy on ImageNet-A/R/S and ObjectNet by 5-10 pp over ERM and 3-6 pp over best baseline without oracle labels.
• Show ∼30% relative reduction in effective-robustness slope gap compared to ERM, indicating better break-line robustness.
• Double the foreground-relevance overlap compared to ERM and outperform Optimizing Relevance Maps without hurting ID accuracy.
• Ablations confirm all three components (counterfactuals, DRO reweighting, relevance regularizer) contribute additively.
Conclusion: SCaRI delivers the first *annotation-free*, generative-counterfactual framework that scales to high-resolution images and substantially mitigates unknown spurious correlations. By uniting diffusion-based interventions, contrastive invariance, adaptive DRO, and explanation-guided regularization, it closes several open gaps left by IRM-style, DRO, and causal-effect methods. Practically, SCaRI can be plugged into any vision backbone and extended to video or multimodal tasks; academically, it offers a testbed for studying causal invariance in the wild and a bridge between generative modeling and causal robustness. Future work can explore online test-time generation of counterfactuals, application to segmentation/detection, and theoretical guarantees linking generative interventions to causal sufficiency.
